title: Machine learning on genomes estimates country-level tuberculosis drug resistance profiles
summary: A validated random forest predicted phenotypic resistance to 12 drugs from whole-genome sequences of 19,149 Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from 29 countries, bias-corrected, to estimate country-level antibiograms; for example, global pooled isoniazid mono-resistance was 10.9%. Compared with a South African national survey, estimates overlapped except isoniazid, ethionamide and second-line injectables (underestimated) and overestimated other drugs among MDR isolates. Convenience genomic sampling.
ai_technology: Previously validated random forest model predicting phenotypic drug resistance from Mtb whole-genome sequences
organization: Boston Children’s Hospital; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Comparison of estimates with a national South African drug-resistance survey.
evidence.unknown: Representativeness of the sampled isolates and accuracy for individual drugs are limited; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest predicted resistance phenotypes that were aggregated into country-level estimates.
